findings.title: runSplitQuery mutates the caller's request.targets via applyTemplateVariables, causing double interpolation and shared-state corruption
findings.body: runSplitQuery now calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, ...) on each target. In the Loki datasource, applyTemplateVariables mutates the passed query object in place (it modifies query.expr and query.step on the original object) rather than returning a copy. Because `request.targets` objects are passed by reference, this mutates the caller's original DataQueryRequest targets. Consequences: (1) when runShardSplitQuery delegates to runSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts line 163), the sub-request targets get interpolated a second time — variables already replaced are re-processed, and any variable whose interpolated value itself contains a variable-like token (e.g. a dashboard variable whose value is '$__interval' or text containing '$var') will be corrupted by double interpolation; (2) the original request object held by the panel/explore is permanently modified, so re-running the query, switching tabs, or the datasource's own metrics/tracking see already-interpolated expressions; (3) the `request` object is also spread into grouped requests (`{ ...request, targets }`) and `request.queryGroupId = uuidv4()` is assigned (line 303), further mutating shared state. The fix is to interpolate on a copy of each query (e.g. `.map((query) => datasource.applyTemplateVariables({ ...query }, ...))`) and to avoid mutating the incoming request.

findings.title: runShardSplitQuery mutates request.targets in place and double-interpolates when delegating to runSplitQuery
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery maps request.targets through datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters). applyTemplateVariables mutates the query object it receives (it rewrites query.expr/query.step in place), so the original request.targets array elements are modified. The interpolated `queries` are then passed to splitQueriesByStreamShard, and each shard sub-request is built as `{ ...request, targets: interpolateShardingSelector(targets, shardsToQuery) }` (line 154) and handed to runSplitQuery (line 163), which — after this PR — interpolates every target again via applyTemplateVariables. This is a double interpolation of the same query objects: any variable value that itself contains a '$'-prefixed token gets re-expanded, producing corrupted LogQL (e.g. a variable value of '$__rate_interval' or a label value containing '$foo' would be substituted again). Additionally, because the objects are shared, the caller's original request is permanently mutated. The interpolation should be done on cloned query objects, and runSplitQuery should not re-interpolate queries that were already interpolated (or runShardSplitQuery should pass the raw targets and let runSplitQuery do the single interpolation).

findings.title: Shard sub-requests spread the original request, re-introducing hidden/empty targets that were filtered out
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery filters targets (removing hidden and empty-expr queries) into `queries` and passes only those to splitQueriesByStreamShard. However, inside runNextRequest the sub-request is built as `{ ...request, targets: interpolateShardingSelector(targets, shardsToQuery) }` — the spread copies the original `request` object, but `targets` is correctly replaced. The problem is that `request` itself was already mutated upstream: runShardSplitQuery's `.map(applyTemplateVariables)` mutated the original target objects in place, and querySplitting.runSplitQuery additionally assigns `request.queryGroupId = uuidv4()` on the request object it receives (which is this same subRequest). More importantly, since the original request.targets objects were mutated in place, any code holding the original request (panel state, query inspector, tracking) now sees interpolated expressions. Also, because the sub-request spreads `request`, properties like `targets` are overridden but the mutation of the shared target objects means the 'filtered' hidden/empty queries in the original request.targets array are also interpolated (they are the same object references), wasting work and mutating queries that should have been skipped. Targets should be cloned before interpolation and the request should not be mutated.

findings.title: runSplitQuery mutates the caller's request by assigning request.queryGroupId
findings.body: Line 303 does `request.queryGroupId = uuidv4();` on the DataQueryRequest passed in by the caller. When runSplitQuery is invoked from runShardSplitQuery (shardQuerySplitting.ts line 163), the `request` is the shard sub-request object created via `{ ...request, targets }` — a shallow copy, so this assignment is contained. But when runSplitQuery is called directly with the panel's original request object, the caller's request is mutated: queryGroupId is overwritten on every invocation. If the same request object is re-used (e.g. re-run, or by the datasource's query() wrapper which may call runSplitQuery and also read request properties), the queryGroupId changes between calls and any code that captured the original request (tracking, request cancellation keyed by requestId/queryGroupId) sees inconsistent state. The request should be treated as immutable; the queryGroupId should be set on a copied request object.

findings.title: applyTemplateVariables is called with request.filters, but the shard-splitting path and other callers may not populate filters consistently; interpolation now happens before querySupportsSplitting checks
findings.body: The new code calls datasource.applyTemplateVariables(query, request.scopedVars, request.filters) at the very start of runSplitQuery, before the queries are partitioned by querySupportsSplitting (which checks isQueryWithRangeVariable(query.expr) for $__range). Previously interpolation happened later (inside runQuery per sub-request), so the $__range check in querySupportsSplitting operated on the raw expression. Now it operates on the interpolated expression. If a query uses $__range, applyTemplateVariables will replace $__range with the full range string (e.g. '5m'/'1h' computed from the whole request range), and isQueryWithRangeVariable will no longer detect it — so the query will incorrectly be treated as splittable and split into 1-day chunks, each of which then gets an incorrect $__range value (the comment on lines 285-286 explicitly warns about this: 'Queries with $__range variable should not be split because then the interpolated $__range variable is incorrect because it is interpolated on the backend with the split timeRange'). The splittability check must run on the pre-interpolation expression, or $__range must be excluded from interpolation before splitting. This is a real correctness regression for queries using $__range with time-based query splitting enabled.

findings.title: Test 'Interpolates queries before running' asserts applyTemplateVariables called 5 times, encoding the double-interpolation behavior as expected
findings.body: The test at line 112 asserts `expect(datasource.applyTemplateVariables).toHaveBeenCalledTimes(5)`. With 1 target and 5 shard groups (4 shard groups + empty shard group), this means applyTemplateVariables is called once per shard sub-request — i.e. the query is interpolated 5 times (once in runShardSplitQuery plus once per runSplitQuery delegation, or once per group). This bakes the repeated/double interpolation into the test suite as the expected behavior. If interpolation is idempotent for simple variables this passes, but it (a) wastes work, and (b) confirms that non-idempotent interpolations (variables whose values contain variable syntax) will be corrupted. The test should assert interpolation happens exactly once per unique query, and a regression test should be added for a variable value containing '$'-syntax to prove double interpolation does not occur.

findings.title: New interpolation test does not cover the $__range splitting-exclusion regression
findings.body: The added test 'Interpolates queries before execution' only verifies that $__auto and $step are replaced in expr and step. It does not cover the interaction with querySupportsSplitting: a query containing $__range must still be excluded from time splitting even though interpolation now happens before the check. Without a test asserting that a query like 'rate({a="b"}[$__range])' is NOT split into multiple runQuery calls (i.e. runQuery called once with the full range), the regression described in querySplitting.ts lines 285-286 (interpolated $__range no longer detected, query incorrectly split, wrong $__range per chunk) would not be caught.
